requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while participating in cycling activities and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. Explain to your counselor how to ride predictably, be conspicuous, think ahead, and ride ready. (b) Show that you know first aid for injuries or illnesses that could occur while cycling, including cuts, scratches, concussions, blisters, sunburn, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, hypothermia, frostbite, dehydration, insect stings, tick bites, and snakebite. Explain to your counselor why you should be able to identify the poisonous plants and poisonous animals that are found in your area.

pamphlet_excerpts: State & Local Bicycle Traffic Laws: However, you should not delay faster drivers unnecessarily (p. 57).
State & Local Bicycle Traffic Laws Principle 2: If you are going the same speed as other vehicles, pull into line with them (p. 57).
State & Local Bicycle Traffic Laws Principle 3: Don't ride too close to the vehicle you are passing (p. 57).
State & Local Bicycle Traffic Laws Principle 4: After you pass, return to the right lane as soon asis convenient (p. 57).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (State & Local Bicycle Traffic Laws): An intersection is any point, including a driveway, where the paths of two vehicles can cross (p. 57).
Step 2 (State & Local Bicycle Traffic Laws): There are ways to get through an intersection as easily and safely as possible (p. 57).
Step 3 (State & Local Bicycle Traffic Laws): First, always move to the lane position that will allow you to ride through most efficiently (p. 57).
Step 4 (State & Local Bicycle Traffic Laws): To turn right, get to the right side; to go straight, stay near the middle; to turn left, move just to the right of the center of the roadway (p. 57).

pamphlet_excerpts: Cycling Apparel, Helmet Fit & Visibility: The Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines are designed to make bicycle riding safer and more enjoyable for you and others (p. 94).

Step 2 (Cycling Apparel, Helmet Fit & Visibility): Assure that tires are fully inflated and brakes are working properly (p. 94).
Step 3 (Cycling Apparel, Helmet Fit & Visibility): Wear clothing that makes you more visible, such as bright neon or fluorescent colors (p. 94).
Step 4 (Cycling Apparel, Helmet Fit & Visibility): Be on the lookout for hazards, such as potholes, broken glass, gravel, puddles, leaves, animals, or anything that could cause you to crash (p. 94).

pamphlet_excerpts: Bicycle Safety Inspection & Maintenance: The Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines are designed to make bicycle riding safer and more enjoyable for you and others (p. 54).
Bicycle Safety Inspection & Maintenance Principle 2: Review these guidelines with your merit badge counselor (p. 54).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Bicycle Safety Inspection & Maintenance): Make sure you can stand over the top tube of your bicycle (p. 54).
Step 2 (Bicycle Safety Inspection & Maintenance): Assure that tires are fully inflated and brakes are working properly (p. 54).
Step 3 (Bicycle Safety Inspection & Maintenance): Wear clothing that makes you more visible, such as bright neon or fluorescent colors (p. 54).
Step 4 (Bicycle Safety Inspection & Maintenance): Be on the lookout for hazards, such as potholes, broken glass, gravel, puddles, leaves, animals, or anything that could cause you to crash (p. 54).

requirements.req_text: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website) (a) Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride. (b) Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride.

sub_requirements.text: Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

pamphlet_excerpts: Road Biking / Trail or Mixed Surface Biking: Using side-to-side bike/body separation, you can control your bike through many tight turns on trails (p. 80).

Road Biking / Trail or Mixed Surface Biking Principle 2: Practice this skill on a relatively flat space with some markers (cones, half tennis balls, or rocks and sticks) and mark out a 90-degree turn (p. 80).
Road Biking / Trail or Mixed Surface Biking Principle 3: Practice riding through the turns several times, increasing your speed, off the saddle and with level pedals (p. 80).
Road Biking / Trail or Mixed Surface Biking Principle 4: Push your bike into the turn, keep your head up and look at your exit point, one finger on each brake lever (p. 80).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Road Biking / Trail or Mixed Surface Biking): On steep climbs a rider may choose one of three positions: seated, crouched, or standing (p. 80).
Step 2 (Road Biking / Trail or Mixed Surface Biking): In the seated position, the rider'sshoulders move forward and the rider may move forward on the saddle (p. 80).
Step 3 (Road Biking / Trail or Mixed Surface Biking): As the terrain becomes steeper, a rider may need to move into a crouched position similar to a ready position (p. 80).
Step 4 (Road Biking / Trail or Mixed Surface Biking): This position provides more power, bike/body separation, and better traction control (p. 80).
